research.abstract: Abstract Background Apolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. However, some individuals have discordant apoB and LDL-C. We evaluated whether apoB/LDL-C discordance is associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a key marker of systemic inflammation, in a nationally representative sample. Methods and Results We analyzed cross-sectional data of 2226 adults aged 20 years or older from the 2015 to 2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete apoB, LDL-C, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). LDL-C and apoB were converted to survey-weighted z scores, and discordance was the residual of apoB regressed on LDL-C. Participants were classified as apoB-high, LDL-C-high, or concordant (reference). The association of discordance group with elevated hs-CRP ( > 3 mg/L) was estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes. Discordance was present in 26.4% of adults (13.7% apoB-higher, 12.6% LDL-C-higher). Elevated hs-CRP prevalence differed by discordance group: 47.6% (95% CI, 37.6–57.7) in the apoB-high group versus 20.5% (12.9–28.1) in the LDL-C-high group and 33.6% (29.7–37.4) in the concordant group. Relative to concordant participants, adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP were higher for apoB-high discordance (odds ratio [OR], 1.58; 95% CI, 1.03–2.45) and lower for LDL-C-high discordance (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30–0.78). Similar results were obtained among participants not on statin therapy, with apoB-high discordance demonstrating stronger adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.01–4.04). Conclusion Discordantly high apoB relative to LDL-C is associated with systemic inflammation in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults.

We evaluated the accuracy of two swab-based nPOC platforms to detect pediatric pulmonary TB. Methods We prospectively enrolled children under 15 years with presumptive TB in Uganda and South Africa. They completed TB evaluation including sputum molecular testing and culture. Two tongue swabs were collected and tested with MiniDock MTB (Pluslife Biotech, China) and Truenat MTB Ultima (Molbio Diagnostics, India), and one swab was dipped in sputum for testing with MiniDock MTB. We calculated the sensitivity and specificity of each index test against a culture-based standard and compared them with sputum molecular testing and smear microscopy. Findings We included 335 children, among whom median age was 3 years (IQR 1-6), 53% were female, 11% were living with HIV, and 16% had microbiologically confirmed TB. Tongue swabs were collected in all children, with invalid test rates of less than 3%. Against a culture-based standard, the sensitivities of tongue swab MiniDock MTB and MTB Ultima were 50% (95% CI 33.4-66.6) and 50% (95% CI 28.2-71.8), respectively, and specificities were ≥98% for both. Sputum swab MiniDock MTB had similar sensitivity to sputum Xpert Ultra (85.7% vs. 75.0%, p=0.45), but substantially higher sensitivity than tongue swab MiniDock MTB (+23.1%, p=0.03) and sputum smear microscopy (+46.4%, p<0.001). Interpretation Sputum swab testing had similar accuracy to sputum Xpert Ultra in children. Tongue swab testing had moderate accuracy, and has value to identify microbiologically confirmed cases when sputum is not available. Funding National Institutes of Health, United States Department of State Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy, and South African Medical Research Council RESEARCH IN CONTEXT Evidence before this study We evaluated the literature from October 2021 to October 2026 for studies in any language on oral swab molecular testing for M. tuberculosis (MTB). We included diagnostic accuracy studies and excluded work on extrapulmonary TB, screening and early assay development, and searched PubMed and Google Scholar with the terms “swab” AND “tuberculosis” AND “diagnosis.” Manual quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) testing on tongue swabs has high accuracy to detect pulmonary TB in adults (80-93% sensitive and >98% specificity), with similar accuracy to sputum samples. Translation to semi-automated PCR assays such as Xpert Ultra have had high specificity but variable sensitivity (59-76%). Newer assays have been developed that are designed specifically for swab testing, and are small, portable, and can be used near the point-of-care (nPOC). Studies in adults have found that nPOC tongue swab testing is feasible, sensitive (75-86%), and specific (>96%). Testing can also be performed by dipping a swab in sputum, offering higher accuracy than tongue swabs and similar performance to sputum Xpert Ultra. However, the evidence in children has been limited to Xpert Ultra tongue swab testing, with low sensitivity (7-19%). Added value of this study To our knowledge, this is the first assessment of two swab-based nPOC assays for childhood TB: MiniDock MTB and MTB Ultima. In two high TB-burden settings of South Africa and Uganda, we prospectively enrolled children with presumptive TB and determined the accuracy of tongue and sputum swab testing. We found that tongue swab testing detected about half of children with culture-confirmed TB; sputum swab testing had substantially higher sensitivity than tongue swabs, and similar performance to sputum Xpert Ultra, meeting the World Health Organization (WHO) target accuracy for an nPOC sputum molecular TB test. Implications of all the available evidence The recent WHO guidelines endorsed sputum swab testing in adults and adolescents, and tongue swabs if sputum is not available. Similarly, we found that a single platform can enable nPOC molecular testing for TB among children, with sputum swab accuracy comparable to Xpert Ultra when sputum is available, and tongue swabs providing a simple, non-invasive approach to increase microbiological confirmation and potentially reduce delays in treatment when sputum is not available.

research.abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 (CYP) genes form a large and functionally diverse superfamily of heme-thiolate monooxygenases that catalyse the oxidation of endogenous and exogenous compounds. Within this superfamily, CYP4 enzymes primarily act on fatty acids, substrates central to energy metabolism. Sustained flight and long distance migration in birds rely on efficient fatty acid use, making CYP4 a pertinent system for examining how lipid associated functions may vary across avian lineages. Here, we characterised the evolution of CYP4 genes across 363 avian whole genomes, representing over 90% of bird families, to investigate patterns of molecular evolution and their association with ecological and life history variation. We identified four CYP4 subfamilies and analysed sequence evolution using site-models, branch-models, and branch-site models. Our analyses revealed conserved elements of the avian CYP4 repertoire alongside lineage-specific heterogeneity in selective constraint. Several amino acid sites under positive selection were located within substrate recognition sites, regions influencing substrate binding and catalysis. Branch-model analyses identified trait-associated variation in selective pressure across feeding habits, migration and primary lifestyle, with gene-specific patterns. Migration-associated differences in ω remained below one, indicating variation in the strength of selective constraint among migration categories. Branch-site analyses revealed evidence of episodic positive selection associated with migratory lineages. Overall, these results highlight site-specific adaptive evolution within CYP4 genes alongside broader variation in selective constraint, providing insight into the evolution of lipid associated metabolic pathways during avian diversification.

research.abstract: Abstract Comparative genomic data can be used to look for substitutions in coding sequences that are associated with the variation of a particular phenotypic trait. A few statistical methods have been proposed to do so for phenotypes represented by discrete values. For continuous traits, no such statistical approach has been proposed, and researchers have resorted to sensible but uncharacterized criteria. Here, we investigate a phylogenetic model for coding sequences where amino acid preferences at a site are given by a continuous function of a quantitative trait. This function is inferred from the amino acids and the trait values in extant species and requires inferred point estimates of ancestral values of the trait at internal nodes. For detecting sites whose evolution is associated with this trait, we use a significance test against the hypothesis that amino acid preference does not depend on the trait. This procedure is compared to simpler strategies on simulated alignments. It displays an increased recall for low false positive rates, which is of special importance for performing whole-genome scans. This comes however at a much higher computational cost, and we suggest using a simple test to filter promising candidate sites. We then revisit a dataset of alignments for 62 species of mammals, using longevity as a phenotypic trait. We apply our method to three protein families that have previously been proposed to display sites associated with variation in lifespan in mammals. Using a graphical representation extracted from the detailed phylogenetic analysis of candidate sites, we suggest that the evidence for this in the sequence data alone is weak. The proposed method has been added to our Pelican software. It is available at https://gitlab.in2p3.fr/phoogle/pelican and can now be used with both discrete and continuous phenotypes to search for sites associated with phenotypic variation, on data sets with thousands of alignments.

research.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Hepatic tuberculosis is a rare extrapulmonary manifestation that may mimic hepatobiliary malignancy or complex cystic lesions, resulting in diagnostic challenges. Case Presentation: A 36-year-old Filipino woman without recognized immunocompromising conditions presented with fever, weight loss, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain. Imaging showed a multiloculated cystic lesion in hepatic segments V/VI with focal biliary prominence. Liver biopsy demonstrated necrotizing and non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with focally positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining. Tissue MTB-PCR detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis without rifampicin resistance, and culture confirmed M. tuberculosis complex susceptible to streptomycin, isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol. CT chest showed diffuse bilateral micronodules in a miliary pattern; initial sputum smear and PCR were negative, but final sputum culture became positive at 6 weeks. Standard 2HRZE/4HR therapy was initiated, with clinical and biochemical improvement at 1 month. Conclusion: Hepatic tuberculosis should be considered in atypical cystic hepatic lesions, and tissue diagnosis is essential to avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

research.abstract: BackgroundLinkage of infectious-disease surveillance data to mortality records is important for estimating long-term outcomes, but incomplete personal identifiers present methodological challenges. We developed and validated a deterministic linkage framework for linking the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System (NTBS) with Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality records. MethodsTB notifications in England from 2001-2024 were linked to ONS mortality records using 12 sequential matching rules based on combinations of NHS number, date of birth, name, postcode, sex and phonetic matching. Linkage outputs underwent person-level deduplication and clerical review. Precision and recall were estimated, and potential linkage bias assessed by variation in identifier completeness and linkage success. Confirmed false-positive links identified during validation were removed from the analytical dataset. ResultsAmong 151,965 TB notifications, 28,060 initial links were identified. Following deduplication, validation and refinement, 26,937 linked notifications were retained. Estimated precision increased from 97.7% to 99.2% (95% CI 96.8-100.0) following removal of false-positive links; estimated recall was 98.1% (95% CI 95.4-98.6%). More than 90% of links used NHS-number-based match keys. PDS enrichment increased NHS-number availability and enabled additional NHS-number-based links, although a small proportion linked to different ONS records following enrichment. NHS number availability and linkage success differed across demographic and social groups, demonstrating differential linkage. ConclusionsA hierarchical deterministic approach combined with targeted validation achieved high linkage accuracy while identifying and addressing differential linkage. This provides a transparent framework for future NTBS-ONS linkage and may be adaptable to other surveillance systems where comparable identifiers are available. research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic susceptibility and directional associations remain unclear. Methods We analyzed European-ancestry genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for ADHD (38,691 cases; 186,843 controls) and BPD (12,339 cases; 1,041,717 controls). Linkage disequilibrium score regression, conjunctional false discovery rate (conjFDR), bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), MR accounting for linkage disequilibrium and sample overlap (MR-LAP), Causal Analysis Using Summary Effect estimates (CAUSE), colocalization, and Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) fine-mapping assessed genetic sharing and directionality. Results Genetic correlation was substantial (r_g = 0.733). ConjFDR identified 48 shared loci; 36 (75%) showed concordant directions in both phenotype-specific comparisons. Functional annotation implicated axon guidance, oxidative phosphorylation, and developing midbrain cells. ADHD-to-BPD MR was positive (22 instruments; inverse-variance weighted beta = 0.487, SE = 0.082, p = 3.27 × 10^-9), persisting after outlier removal, MR-LAP correction, and exclusion of two instruments at colocalized loci. Reverse MR was positive (five instruments; beta = 0.303, SE = 0.112, p = 6.83 × 10^-3) but heterogeneous and variant-sensitive. CAUSE favored directional over sharing-only models in both directions (delta ELPD = 6.98 and 5.92, respectively). SuSiE colocalization supported shared signals at rs17576773, rs9969232, and rs4727799. Conclusions ADHD and BPD exhibit extensive genetic overlap involving 48 shared loci and convergent evidence of directional associations. Findings across complementary methods more consistently support an ADHD-to-BPD relationship, suggesting that shared genetic susceptibility alone may not fully explain their co-occurrence.

research.abstract: Background Aging-related genes (ARGs) may contribute to immune heterogeneity in tuberculosis (TB), but their diagnostic and biological relevance remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify TB-associated ARG transcripts, characterize their immune and molecular correlates, and evaluate their exploratory diagnostic performance across prespecified cohorts. Patients and methods Public TB transcriptomic cohorts were analyzed together with a local bulk RNA-seq cohort comprising 5 TB patients and 5 controls and a local single-cell RNA-seq cohort comprising 3 active TB patients and 3 controls. The local cohorts were selected using random sampling. Age-adjusted differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine-learning-based feature selection, immune-infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, single-cell annotation, and Comparative Toxicogenomics Database-based compound-gene screening were performed. Results GSE83456 included 45 TB patients and 61 controls. Age-adjusted differential expression identified 189 differentially expressed genes, and the intersection of DEGs, ARGs, and blue-module genes yielded 11 discovery candidates. Nested model selection in GSE83456 identified a naive Bayes classifier based on STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14. Across five repeated stratified nested cross-validation runs, the mean AUC was 0.962, with a repeat-level range of 0.954-0.969. Balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 0.926, 0.911, 0.941, and 0.928, respectively. Exploratory evaluations included GSE19439, GSE34608, GSE62525, GSE19444, and the local RNA-seq cohort. Consensus clustering separated TB samples into two ARG-associated subgroups with distinct immune-infiltration and pathway-activity profiles. CIBERSORT analysis identified significant TB-control differences in 9 of 22 inferred immune-cell types. Single-cell analysis demonstrated heterogeneous expression of STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14 across annotated immune-cell subsets. CTD screening generated exploratory compound-gene associations that provide testable hypotheses for future experimental studies. Conclusion Age-adjusted multi-cohort analysis identified candidate ARG-associated TB markers and immune patterns. STAT1, PLAUR, JAK2, and P2RY14 are candidate markers rather than clinically validated biomarkers and require independent experimental and clinical validation.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the causative agent of tuberculosis (TB) is able to survive and replicate within host cells of the myeloid cell lineage, a critical step in the development of active TB, achieved through multiple immune evasion mechanisms. TRPML1 (Mucolipin 1), a non-selective Ca 2+ ion channel belonging to the TRP superfamily, is predominantly expressed in innate immune cells and is localized intracellularly along the endosomal-lysosomal continuum. TRPML1-mediated Ca 2+ signalling is vital for lysosomal biogenesis and trafficking processes essential for effective immune responses. The mechanisms regulating TRPML1 channel function in myeloid cells during mycobacterial infection remain poorly characterized. METHODS: During in vitro infection, TRPML1 expression was modulated in a time-dependent manner by Mtb and M. bovis BCG in murine macrophages, as well as in human neutrophils (PMNs) and macrophages (MDMs). Using pharmacological modulation of TRPML1 channel activity, we observed alterations in intracellular Ca 2+ concentrations following Mtb infection. RESULTS: Here, we describe distinct TRPML1 expression patterns in granulomas from TB patients who had completed treatment for active TB, suggesting a potential role for TRPML1 in pathogenesis. We further demonstrate that Mtb infection is associated with altered TRPML1 expression and intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis, accompanied by changes in ROS production, necrotic cell death and enhanced mycobacterial survival within host cells. Treatment of PMN-MDM cocultures with a TRPML1 antagonist, but not an agonist, was associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and necrotic cell death. DISCUSSION: Here, we show that Mtb-mediated disruption of TRPML1 function is associated with altered intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis and may contribute to impaired phagosome maturation, a process previously linked to TRPML1-dependent endolysosomal function, thereby potentially favoring mycobacterial survival within host cells. These findings suggest that Mtb-induced alterations in TRPML1 associated cellular Ca²⁺ homeostasis may impair Ca²⁺-dependent ROS production and cell death, potentially affecting intracellular Mtb survival. Our findings support a role for TRPML1 in maintaining myeloid cell Ca²⁺ homeostasis and suggest that TRPML1 may contribute to the innate immune response to Mtb infection.

research.abstract: Character recoding is a common practice in evolutionary studies. For example, phylogenies can be inferred from protein-coding DNA sequences via 61-state codon substitution models. However, often the inference is instead done by adopting 20-state amino acid replacement models that do not explicitly consider synonymous substitution. When there is substantial heterogeneity of amino acid frequencies among sites and/or among lineages, another sort of character recoding is sometimes performed. In these cases, one option is to reduce the state space of the model by placing each of the 20 amino acids into one of a relatively small number (e.g., 6) of groups of amino acids and then modeling only how group membership changes at a site over evolutionary time. Unfortunately, these kinds of character recoding schemes are prone to reducing the amount of available evolutionary information. Here, we provide a likelihood framework to statistically assess recoding schemes. Although we concentrate on the recoding of 61-state codon substitution models into 20-state amino acid replacement models, the general approach is also relevant to other recoding schemes such as those that recode 20-state models into 6-state models.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic-related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS-CoV-2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory-clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto–Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative-binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non-linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0–12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0–12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822–1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868–1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV–NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment-wide threshold. Conclusions We identified a modest pandemic-era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

research.abstract: Abstract There is a need to breed superior wheat cultivars to meet increasing global food demand. However, modern cultivars have undergone a substantial loss of genetic diversity due to intensive breeding. A pool of genetic diversity remains untapped in wheat landraces and analysis against a single reference cannot detect genes that the reference lacks. Pangenomics can help identify genes of potential agronomic importance in these old lines that can be applied to accelerate wheat improvement. Here, we have constructed the largest wheat pangenome to date, representing 1,061 diverse individuals (827 landraces and 234 modern cultivars) from 47 countries across six continents. We identified 10,426 predicted gene models specific to landraces that are enriched for functions associated with disease resistance, abiotic stress adaptation, and symbiosis, as well as 176 landrace-specific candidate disease resistance loci. Phylogenetic analysis inferred from gene presence/absence variation reflects SNP-based ancestry-associated structure, while independent Iso-Seq data from 14 cultivars showed 96.4% concordance with cultivar-specific gene presence calls from our PAV analysis, supporting the robustness of the resource. Our results reveal that landraces harbour an extensive repertoire of genes that are absent from modern wheat cultivars and provide a foundational resource that links this gene content variation to specific accessions and ancestral groups, enabling candidate genes to be prioritised in donor lines for subsequent introgression and supporting the systematic reintroduction of adaptive variation to enhance wheat resilience and sustainability in the face of climate change.

research.abstract: Abstract Infectious diseases continue to pose a global health challenge, intensified by antimicrobial resistance and limitations of pharmaceutical countermeasures. Nanotechnology offers a promising front against these barriers using intelligent, multifunctional systems. This review explores the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), CRISPR gene editing, bacteriophage therapy, and immune modulation within the framework of second-generation nanoparticle therapeutics. AI-guided modelling enables predictive optimization of nanoparticle design on the basis of size, charge, and surface proteins, targeting specific pathogens and providing enhanced stability. Consequently, nanoparticles serve as precision nanocarriers and protective delivery vehicles for the CRISPR-Cas system, shielding nucleic acid cargo from enzymatic degradation and enabling targeted intracellular delivery via pH-responsive endosomal escape mechanisms. The nanoparticles not only provide protection but also enable tissue-targeting and infection-site-specific delivery of the CRISPR-Cas system, facilitating precise genome editing to reverse resistance in specific pathogens such as HIV and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Phage nanoparticle hybrids further expand antimicrobial potency by enhancing phage stability, delivery, and host range. Moreover, engineered nanoparticles modulate the immune system via immunosuppressive and immunostimulant strategies for reducing hyperinflammation and enhancing pathogen clearance, respectively. Despite such encouraging laboratory outcomes, the clinical translation of AI-integrated nanoparticle platforms still faces a number of obstacles. Large-scale manufacturing, scalability, and reproducibility pose a significant challenge. Regulatory approvals for such multi-modal nano-drugs seem to get bogged down due to vague and scarce exemplary proofs. Furthermore, safety and efficacy apprehensions, unpredictable and complex host-phage interactions, cost-effectiveness, and equitable access remain a subject matter of concern. Conclusively, the convergence of advanced nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and synthetic biology marks the dawn of a transformative era in infectious disease therapeutics where treatment is not only intelligent and adaptive but also ethically and globally inclusive. research.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prevalence and evolution of drug resistance in TB pose a persistent threat to global TB control. Understanding the epidemiological characteristics, population distribution, and temporal trends of drug resistance is crucial for evaluating the effectiveness of prevention and control measures and adjusting strategies accordingly. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed 9,665 clinical isolates of Mycobacterium TB collected between 2015 and 2024. Drug susceptibility testing was performed using the proportion method to detect resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, streptomycin, and levofloxacin. The chi-square test was used to compare differences between groups, and the chi-square test for trend was applied to analyze temporal changes in drug resistance. RESULTS: The overall drug resistance rate was 20.87% (2017/9665, 95% CI: 20.06%-21.69%), and the MDR rate was 10.25% (991/9665, 95% CI: 9.66%-10.88%). Drug resistance rates varied significantly among different populations, with males (1528/6730,22.70%; 95% CI: 21.71%-23.72%) exhibiting higher rates than females (489/2935,16.66%; 95% CI: 15.33%-18.06%), and the 19-59 age group (1511/6788,22.26%; 95% CI: 21.27%-23.27%) showing higher rates than the ≤ 18 (124/694,17.87%; 95% CI: 15.09%-20.92%) and ≥ 60 age groups (382/2183, 17.50%; 95% CI: 15.93%-19.16%). Over the ten-year period, the overall drug resistance rate showed a significant upward trend (from 17.29% to 22.98%). Rates of single drug resistance, PDR, and resistance to streptomycin and levofloxacin also increased significantly. In contrast, the MDR rate and resistance rates to rifampicin and ethambutol did not show significant trends. CONCLUSION: The TB drug resistance problem in this region is severe, with a rapid increase in resistance to the key second-line drug levofloxacin, indicating significant challenges for the current prevention and control system. Targeted interventions for populations with higher resistance rates, such as males and young adults, along with strengthened antibiotic stewardship, are critical to curbing the further spread of drug resistance.

research.abstract: Abstract Micromonas polaris is the dominant picoeukaryote of the Arctic Ocean, where it sustains primary production across habitats from sea ice to open water to the subsurface chlorophyll maximum. How a single species maintains this ecological breadth has remained unclear. Standard phylogenetic markers such as 18S rRNA are nearly invariant within M. polaris and conceal any internal genomic heterogeneity the species may possess. Here we present a pangenome of 14 M. polaris strains spanning the Arctic basin, integrated with Tara Oceans metagenomes, that resolves the species into two diverged ecotypes invisible to 18S rRNA but recovered consistently by prp8 , genome-wide SNPs, ANI, and orthogroup-based phylogenies. The two ecotypes coexist sympatrically, with one lineage consistently enriched deeper in the water column across the basin. M. polaris carries 990 polar-specific hierarchical orthogroups absent from temperate Micromonas , organised around one-carbon metabolism, endocytosis, transmembrane transport, and photo-oxidative stress response. Several components show phylogenetic signatures of horizontal acquisition from co-occurring marine taxa. Atlantification is bringing temperate Micromonas into Arctic margins seasonally, but the polar night likely limits their year-round persistence. M. polaris and its polar-specific toolkit appear positioned to persist through the dark season, suggesting Arctic margins will undergo seasonal turnover rather than stable replacement.

research.abstract: Abstract Introgression introduced deeply diverged archaic variation into modern human populations and contributed to local adaptation. In Indigenous American populations, however, the landscape of adaptive introgression remains poorly resolved. Genome-wide scans have reported numerous candidate loci, but complex demographic histories and recent admixture make genuine signals difficult to distinguish from false positives. Here, we systematically re-evaluated previously reported candidates of adaptive introgression in Peruvians using a multilayered framework and refined more than 150 putative signals to 25 high-confidence candidate loci with concordant evidence of Neanderthal- or Denisovan-like ancestry and positive selection. Using ancestral recombination graph (ARG) approaches, we inferred selection onset windows for 21 loci. These onsets were non-uniformly distributed across Peruvian population history, revealing temporally dynamic selection without robust evidence for a fixed number of discrete waves. Together with pre-Columbian ancient DNA evidence, the inferred histories support the inheritance of the candidate adaptive archaic haplotypes through ancestral Native American populations rather than first introduction through post-Columbian admixture. Functional analyses identified network-level signals consistent with polygenic selection in lipid metabolic and immune-related pathways, elevated regulatory effects predicted across archaic haplotypes, and occasional coding variation of potential functional relevance, including a missense variant at the immune-related gene CXCR4 . Our results show that archaic introgressed variation remained evolutionarily important and available to selection long after introgression, providing a reservoir of genetic variation that could be repeatedly recruited by selection at different points in American population history. Significance Statement Archaic variants reached the Americas through populations already carrying Neanderthal and Denisovan ancestry, offering an opportunity to study adaptation far from the original contact zone. Scans of American populations have reported more putative adaptive introgression loci than realistically expected, partly because the complex demographic histories make true signals difficult to distinguish from false positives. Reconstructing selection histories at credible loci may in turn help constrain that history. Here we identify 25 high-confidence candidate regions in Peruvians, among which 21 have inferred selection onsets predating European contact, and archaic-associated alleles from all 25 are present in pre-Columbian American ancient genomes. Functional analyses find pathway-level selection signals, predicted regulatory effects, and occasional evolutionarily interesting missense variants, including at the immune-related gene CXCR4 .

research.abstract: Introduction TB incidence in Suriname has remained stable over the last decade. Understanding transmission patterns is essential for developing effective TB control strategies to interrupt ongoing transmission. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of routinely collected demographic and clinical data combined with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. Patients were classified into large (>6 patients) clusters, small (2-6 patients) clusters, or as non-clustered cases (unique). Bivariate and multivariable analyses compared patients in large clusters with those in small clusters and non-clustered patients. Epidemiological links obtained through patient interviews were compared with WGS findings. Results Of 698 TB patients notified during 2019-2024, WGS data were available for 368 (53%); 85% belonged to a genomic cluster. Indigenous ethnicity was inversely associated with membership in a large versus a small cluster (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.1-0.6). Compared with non-clustered cases, patients in large clusters were more likely to report illicit drug use (aOR = 3.0; 95% CI = 1.1-8.9). Conclusion WGS provided detailed insights into Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission in Suriname. Illicit drug use was associated with membership in large transmission clusters, highlighting the need for early case finding and strengthened collaboration between TB and substance-use services.

research.abstract: Ancestral sequences and substitution histories are usually averaged out in phylogenetic inference and are therefore not reported to the user. However, they can be recovered through ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic character mapping. By implementing and validating a new ASR and stochastic mapping package compatible with both single-locus and multispecies coalescent analysis, we show how reconstructing substitution histories can enhance the information gained about the tempo and mode of molecular evolution. We observe that known substitution histories (simulated and empirical) are recovered more accurately and precisely on time trees compared with unconstrained and non-ultrametric substitution trees that lack temporal directionality (maximum likelihood and Bayesian). We show that codon-partition models with site-rate heterogeneity, based on the four nucleotide characters, can effectively approximate the histories of synonymous and non-synonymous change, while requiring far less runtime than computationally demanding codon models that require 61 characters. In turn, this provides low-bias estimation of dN/dS that is robust to non-stationarity in GC content, codon usage bias, and nucleotide exchangeability rates. Lastly, using three case studies, we demonstrate how the approach can recover expected patterns in molecular evolution and pathogen transmission: that i) smaller-bodied mammalian species tend to have faster synonymous substitution rates than larger relatives, ii) amino acid substitutions are correlated with 3Di structural changes in aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and iii) influenza A virus spread more frequently to nearby locations than distant ones, in a major H3N2 outbreak in New Zealand. These three trends were more pronounced when based on count estimates derived from stochastic mapping, relative to parametric rates and distances. Our open-source code comes with a user-friendly graphical interface, as the BeastMap package for BEAST 2; supporting a wide range of clock, site, and tree models and data types - including insertions and deletions - within a Bayesian phylogenetic framework.

research.abstract: Abstract Metabarcoding has transformed our view of marine protist communities, yet many sequences in environmental surveys are not assigned confident taxonomic identity. These taxonomically ambiguous sequences may include lineages that are not within any known eukaryotic supergroup, which we refer to here as orphan lineages. These orphan lineages matter beyond taxonomy-based community analyses, because they can help us understand early eukaryotic evolution. Here we used phylogenetic inferences and sequence similarity networks (SSNs) of long-read metabarcoding data of the ribosomal operon (18S-28S rDNA) to identify three novel phylum-level orphan lineages. We designate these lineages Deep Orphan Lineages 1-3 (DEEPOLs) and show that they are exclusively marine and part of the rare biosphere, yet ecologically distinct: DEEPOL1 is a cosmopolitan generalist, DEEPOL2 a conditionally rare lineage capable of local polar blooms, and DEEPOL3 a non-polar lineage with a tendency toward the dark ocean. For DEEPOL2, lineage-specific digital PCR (dPCR) combined with catalyzed reporter deposition fluorescence in situ hybridization (CARD-FISH) provides the first in situ visualization of these cells, revealing small, flagellated, and morphologically inconspicuous protists. Together, our results show that substantial diversity remains hidden among rare lineages, and that long-read sequencing combined with targeted molecular and microscopy approaches offers a first step toward linking orphan sequences to organisms and their evolution and ecological roles.

research.abstract: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct species for 80.3% and 66.6% of cellular and viral queries, and the function head the correct gene family for 97.3% and 97.2%, reaching 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark. Across all three benchmarks MicroDUET outranked 17 other genomic encoders. Without training on lineage, clade or drug-susceptibility tasks, MicroDUET identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mpox virus lineages and clades (0.965, 0.975 accuracy), discriminated rifampicin resistance without lineage adjustment (AUROC 0.985), and retrospectively identified an emerging mpox lineage as anomalous (AUROC 0.974). MicroDUET operates 10^3 - 10^4 times faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments. MicroDUET therefore provides a compact, reusable representation for scalable pathogen surveillance and sequence triage.

research.abstract: Empyema necessitans is a rare complication of pleural infection in which infected pleural fluid extends through the parietal pleura into the surrounding soft tissues. We report the case of a 32-year-old man of Indian origin living in the United Kingdom who presented with worsening right-sided pleuritic chest pain, several months of night sweats, and a persistent dry cough. Five months earlier, he had been treated for right-sided pneumonia complicated by a pleural effusion, with persistent radiographic abnormalities on follow-up. Examination revealed reduced right-sided air entry and a tender, fluctuant swelling over the right posterior chest wall. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a posterior pleural collection extending through the chest wall into the adjacent paraspinal musculature, consistent with empyema necessitans. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yielded frank purulent fluid. Routine bacterial, anaerobic, and fungal cultures were negative. Acid-fast bacilli were not seen on initial microscopy; however, mycobacterial culture became positive after seven days, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of the pleural fluid detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Whole-genome sequencing subsequently identified a lineage 1 East-African-Indian-Ocean isolate with predicted susceptibility to first-line antituberculous agents. Four-drug antituberculous therapy was commenced, with subsequent clinical and radiological improvement. This case highlights chest wall swelling as an unusual presentation of tuberculosis and emphasizes the importance of cross-sectional imaging and targeted mycobacterial testing in establishing the diagnosis.

research.abstract: Polygonatum zanlanscianense Pamp. is a perennial herb (Asparagaceae) endemic to China, whose rhizomes are used in folk medicine as a substitute for Polygonati Rhizoma. Although its plastome has been reported, the mitogenome remained uncharacterized. Here, we assembled and annotated the complete linear mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense and analysed its gene repertoire, codon usage, repeats, RNA editing sites, MTPTs, synteny, phylogeny and Ka/Ks. The 689,491-bp mitogenome (GC 46.23%) encodes 56 genes: 36 PCGs, three rRNA genes and 17 tRNA genes. Codon usage is biased toward A/U-ending codons. We identified 68 SSRs, 25 tandem repeats, 1366 dispersed repeat pairs, 585 predicted C-to-U editing sites concentrated at the first and second codon positions, and 30 MTPT fragments accounting for 2.24% of the mitogenome. Phylogenetic analysis placed P. zanlanscianense as sister to Polygonatum kingianum Collett & Hemsl. Median Ka/Ks was below 1 for 33 of the 35 genes analysed; although rpl5 and ccmB showed elevated ratios, branch-site tests did not support positive selection. This first mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense provides genomic resources for comparative genomic, phylogenetic and medicinal studies in Polygonatum.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis Diagnosis delays among tuberculosis patients can worsen infection transmission, disease severity, and mortality risk. Identifying factors influencing delays is crucial due to its persistence across healthcare levels and communities. The study identify determinants of tuberculosis diagnosis delay among patients attending public health facility of Metekel zone, Northwest Ethiopia:2023 Methods An unmatched case-control study was conducted in Metekel zone health facilities from March to April 2023, involving 210 tuberculosis patients (103 cases, 107 controls) selected through systematic sampling. Data collected through structured questionnaires and STATA used for analysis, including bi-variable and multi-variable logistic regressions. Variables with p-value < 0.25 in bi-variable analysis were included in the final model after checking model fitness and multicollinearity. Results Overall, 210 tuberculosis patients were included in the study. The following independent variables were associated diagnosis delay of tuberculosis: TB patients who travel greater than 10km (AOR: 2.941, (95 % CI: 1.509, 5.731); TB patients who are living at rural area (AOR: 4.135, 95 % CI :1.759, 9.723); TB patients who prior visit in holly-water and traditional medicine [AOR: 2.978, (95% CI: 1.292, 6.863); poor knowledge about TB [AOR: 2.826, (95% CI: 1.404, 5.687)]. Conclusion Tuberculosis diagnosis delay is a major challenge to eliminate tuberculosis by breaking the chain of transmission. This study can be attributed to factors including place of residence being rural, poor knowledge about tuberculosis, non-health facility initial actions upon symptom onset, and far distance to health institutions. Recognizing these determinants helps in identifying and addressing barriers inhibiting early diagnosis, potentially improving healthcare access and promoting more timely diagnosis and treatment for tuberculosis patients.

research.abstract: Abstract Objectives Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway infections can persist for years despite intensive antibiotic therapy guided by standard antimicrobial susceptibility testing. While this technique captures the emergence of resistance, it does not reproduce many features of the infection environment, where adaptation acquired during chronic infection may alter bacterial responses to antibiotics in ways that are not fully reflected by conventional susceptibility testing. Here we investigated antibiotic responses of longitudinal clinical isolates under standard laboratory conditions and in an airway epithelial infection model. Methods Six longitudinal pairs of P. aeruginosa isolates from people with cystic fibrosis were analysed. Changes in bacterial growth following exposure to tobramycin, ceftazidime and ciprofloxacin were quantified under standard laboratory conditions and compared with changes in bacterial burden after treatment measured in differentiated airway epithelial cultures maintained under air-liquid interface (ALI) conditions that reproduce key features of the airway infection environment. Representative phenotypes were visualized by confocal microscopy and interpreted in the context of available whole-genome sequencing data. Results Major resistance phenotypes identified by conventional susceptibility testing were largely reproduced in the ALI model. However, concordance between phenotypes observed under standard laboratory and ALI conditions differed between antibiotics. Several isolates classified as susceptible according to conventional susceptibility testing displayed substantial survival in the ALI model, and these discordant phenotypes were observed predominantly among those isolates recovered after prolonged airway persistence. Genomic analyses identified mutations associated with both classical resistance mechanisms and chronic adaptation. Conclusions Phenotypes observed under conventional laboratory conditions do not uniformly predict those observed in the ALI airway conditions. Discordant phenotypes were most apparent among chronically adapted isolates and varied between antibiotics, suggesting that adaptation acquired during chronic infection can alter antibiotic responses in ways that are not fully reflected by conventional susceptibility testing.

research.abstract: Importance: Standard repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation protocols are difficult to integrate into inpatient psychiatric care because they require daily treatment over several weeks. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) may offer a feasible augmentation strategy for hospitalized patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Objective: To determine whether connectivity-guided accelerated iTBS improves depressive symptoms beyond routine multimodal inpatient care in hospitalized patients with TRD. Design, Setting, and Participants: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial was conducted in the inpatient unit of the Department of Psychiatry, University of Oldenburg, Karl-Jaspers-Klinik, Bad Zwischenahn, Germany. Patients aged 18 to 65 years with unipolar TRD were recruited between May 2021 and August 2024. Interventions: Participants received active or sham iTBS targeting an individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex site showing strongest functional anticorrelation with the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex using resting-state functional MRI. Treatment was delivered as 3 daily sessions over 10 weekdays (30 sessions; 54 000 pulses total) as augmentation to routine multimodal inpatient care. Main Outcomes and Measures: Primary and secondary outcomes were changes in Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores assessed weekly and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores assessed daily during the 2-week stimulation phase. Exploratory outcomes included response and remission rates. Results: Of 57 randomized participants, 51 completed treatment (active, n=27; sham, n=24). The cohort exhibited moderate-to-severe treatment resistance (mean Maudsley Staging Method score, 10.9) and psychiatric comorbidity in 82% of participants. Active iTBS was associated with steeper MADRS improvement than sham (-3.54 points/week; 95% CI, -5.53 to -1.55; false discovery rate-adjusted P<.001), corresponding to model-estimated reductions of 12.06 versus 4.98 points (Cohen d=-0.89). BDI-II trajectories similarly favored active treatment, although with a smaller effect size (-0.23 points/day; 95% CI, -0.41 to -0.05; false discovery rate-adjusted P=.02; Cohen d=0.22). MADRS response rates were higher with active iTBS (42.3% vs 13.0%), whereas remission rates were numerically but not significantly greater (26.9% vs 12.5%). No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusions and Relevance: Accelerated connectivity-guided iTBS produced significant add-on antidepressant effects during acute inpatient treatment of TRD. Larger multicenter trials are needed to establish durability and optimize clinical implementation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04832750 .

research.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

research.abstract: Retrospective reassessment of archival brain banks provides opportunities to identify previously undocumented neuropathologies. However, limited tissue availability and preservation, together with differences in sampling and staining protocols across brain banks, can constrain the histological information available for analysis. This study investigated whether computational models can integrate complementary information across histological stains and retain discriminative information under incomplete stain availability. A deep learning model incorporating shared-specific feature modeling, cross-stain knowledge distillation, and random modality masking was developed and evaluated on 1,607 whole slide images from the dorsolateral frontal cortex of 602 donors across three cohorts. Using chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) and their comorbidity as a proof-of-principle application, our model achieved macro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.899, 0.904, and 0.898 across three stain-defined groups, exceeding corresponding single-stain baselines. Discriminative performance was retained when each group's defining stain was withheld. Model-predicted disease probabilities were associated with neuropathological staging measures for AD and CTE, and spatial attribution patterns on the remaining stains were largely preserved under defining-stain masking. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of leveraging complementary and partially overlapping histopathological information under incomplete stain availability, providing a foundation for future computational studies across brain regions and brain banks.

research.abstract: Abstract Organismal development, homeostasis and immunity are facilitated by distinct forms of regulated cell death (RCD). These include conserved apoptosis and necroptosis, a proposed backup antimicrobial defence that requires RIPK3-mediated activation of MLKL and is predicted to be absent in several species lacking MLKL. Zebrafish studies have identified a RIPK3-dependent regulated necrosis that is distinct from necroptosis and is pathogenic in tuberculosis. Here, we experimentally confirm the bioinformatics-based prediction that zebrafish lack canonical necroptosis because they lack MLKL, despite retaining functional RIPK3. We take advantage of the finding that Caspase-8 promotes apoptosis while restraining necroptosis; its deficiency is embryonic lethal in mice unless RIPK3 or MLKL is also inhibited. In contrast, we found that Caspase-8-deficient zebrafish are viable through adulthood without obvious morphological defects. Inhibition of related caspases did not compromise viability, arguing against functional redundancy. Finally, Ripk3 overexpression failed to induce death in Caspase-8-deficient embryos. Our work highlights the zebrafish as a model for exploring RIPK3 and extrinsic apoptosis biology in disease contexts in the natural absence of canonical necroptotic execution. Summary statement Cell death drives many pathological conditions. Using casp8 mutant zebrafish, we show that zebrafish lack canonical necroptosis despite retaining functional RIPK3.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Circulating fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises dramatically in chronic kidney disease, particularly in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). At high concentrations, and with declining Klotho, FGF23 has been linked to renal inflammation. The cell types and transcriptional programs mediating these off-target actions remain undefined. We asked whether the diseased kidney responds to FGF23 differently from the healthy kidney, and whether any disease-specific response could be targeted. Methods Male and female DBA/2J mice received streptozotocin or vehicle to induce DKD. On day 56, mice received a single dose intravenous injection of FGF23 (0.3 µg) or vehicle, with tissue collected 1 h later for single-nucleus RNA sequencing, differential expression and regulon (inferred transcription factor activity) analysis. Candidate pathways were tested in precision-cut kidney slices using the CEBPB inhibitor ST-101. Results Streptozotocin-treated male mice developed early DKD with a 6-fold increase in urinary albumin/creatinine ratio and 50% higher blood urea nitrogen with preserved glomerular filtration rate. All major renal cell types were annotated. Canonical FGF23 signaling was intact in disease, with segment-specific target induction conserved in both conditions (e.g. Cyp24a1 in PT-S1 and DCT1). Superimposed on this were disease-restricted responses, including Wsb1 in DCT1 and Pdk4 in PT-S2, PST, DCT1 and DCT2. Regulon analysis revealed DKD-specific induction of CEBPB regulon activity by FGF23 across all analyzed tubular segments, and of STAT1 in several segments. Pre-treatment with a CEBPB inhibitor suppressed CEBPB activity, downstream NF-κB and pro-inflammatory gene sets, and immune-like cell abundance in diseased slices. Conclusion In the diabetic kidney, FGF23 engages a STAT1-CEBPB-NF-κB axis absent from healthy kidney and extending beyond its canonical Klotho-dependent target segments, identifying CEBPB as a potential treatment target for FGF23’s pathological inflammatory actions.

research.abstract: SUMMARY Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading infectious cause of death, with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) challenging disease control. Brazil has a high TB burden, and Rio Grande do Sul state reports persistently high incidence and drug-resistance rates. The drivers shaping the regional DR-TB burden remain poorly characterised. Methods We conducted genomic surveillance of confirmed DR-TB cases in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from January 2023 to September 2024. Clinical isolates underwent genotypic (gDST) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We analyzed 33 newly sequenced genomes and 267 historical Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes collected in 2011–2019 to characterize resistance, transmission, and spatiotemporal patterns and estimate the contributions of transmitted and acquired rifampicin resistance. Findings Molecular testing detected rifampicin resistance missed by pDST, including borderline rpoB mutations in 18.2% and emerging resistance-associated variants in 3% of the 33 analyzed isolates. Conversely, pDST detected baseline bedaquiline resistance missed by WGS in one newly diagnosed case. Among 300 genomes, 181 (60.3%) clustered into 32 genomic clusters at a 5-SNP threshold, including 12 with long-term circulation and several spanning prisons and communities. Sublineage frequencies remained stable over time, whereas we observed marked geographic structuring and localized clonal expansion. Among 178 rifampicin-resistant isolates, transmission accounted for an estimated 79.2–88.2% of resistance, corresponding to 11.8–20.8% of cases arising through de novo acquisition during treatment. Interpretation Our findings identify active transmission as the main driver of rifampicin-resistant TB in Rio Grande do Sul, with long-term transmission chains extending across both incarcerated and community settings. These results underscore the urgent need to strengthen timely TB case detection and resistance testing, enhance contact investigations, and implement targeted interventions aiming to interrupt persistent transmission chains.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first–line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross–sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact test. Results Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30–40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood–stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood–stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Abstract Amoeboid ochrophytes (stramenopiles) exhibit diverse cell forms and plastid states, yet many lineages are known primarily from environmental sequences. We describe Leucomyxa quisqueyensis sp. nov., a freshwater amoeboid ochrophyte isolated from a freshwater drainage channel in La Chinola, Santo Domingo Oeste, Dominican Republic. In established cultures, the isolate consistently formed extensive multinucleate reticula, with fine strands linking densely branched regions. The largest networks exceeded 2 mm. Confocal imaging revealed longitudinal microtubule strands along the reticulopodia. Rounded cysts measured 6.47–15.43 µm in diameter. SSU rRNA and nuclear phylogenomic analyses identified Leucomyxa plasmidifera as the closest sampled named relative. Their sister relationship received 100% ultrafast bootstrap support in the phylogeny inferred from 124 nuclear protein markers. The two species differed by 2.50% across comparable SSU rRNA positions and by 15.26% across 25,619 comparable amino-acid positions in the nuclear marker alignment. Transcripts with similarity to Tic110 and PPP1, together with matches to plastome-derived protein queries, support the hypothesis that L. quisqueyensis retains a cryptic plastid. The new species adds a cultured Caribbean freshwater representative to Leucomyxa and provides a basis for comparing reticulopodial organization and plastid evolution among closely related amoeboid ochrophytes.

research.abstract: Abstract Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with ω₀ > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with ω₀ > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.
